question: A 37-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after being attacked with a knife. Physical examination shows a 4-cm laceration in the midline of the right forearm. An MRI of the right arm shows damage to a nerve that runs between the superficial and deep flexor digitorum muscles. Loss of sensation over which of the following areas is most likely in this patient?

options.opa: Palmar surface of the little finger

analysis: The nerve that runs between the superficial and deep flexor digitorum muscles in the forearm is the median nerve. Damage to the median nerve typically results in loss of sensation in the palmar surface of the lateral three and a half fingers (thumb, index, middle, and half of the ring finger) and the corresponding area on the dorsal side of the fingertips. The little finger is innervated by the ulnar nerve, and the lateral aspect of the forearm is also innervated by the radial nerve. Therefore, the area most likely to experience loss of sensation due to median nerve damage is the palmar surface of the little finger, which is innervated by the ulnar nerve, making it the least likely option. The correct answer is the palmar surface of the little finger, as it is not affected by median nerve damage.
